items.title: Resources: a capacity, a queue and a lease
items.criterion: src/resources.js gives a resource a name, a capacity, a scope and a first-come queue. Machine scope lives under PULLBOARD_HOME, so every repo on the machine shares it; repo scope lives in the git common directory. Taking a resource returns at once when a place is free, and otherwise waits in line, reporting the holders and its place. Giving it back frees the place for the next in line. A holder whose process dies frees its place within 60 seconds, and a waiter whose process died is skipped, so nothing waits forever. pullboard resources lists each resource with its capacity, its holders (agent, repo, since) and its line. Tests use real separate processes: with capacity 1, three takers run strictly in arrival order; a holder killed with SIGKILL frees its place within 60 seconds; a waiter killed in line is skipped; two repos on one machine share a machine-scoped resource. The gate passes.

items.title: A worktree's unmerged code never migrates the shared board
items.criterion: Every worktree shares one board in the git common directory, so a migration in unmerged code (a schema bump on a branch) used to rewrite the shared board as soon as that branch's gate or spec check ran. Opening the shared board anywhere in src/ outside the view's server (which is #148's), including src/relay.js's localRecords, refuses to migrate it when the running code's schema version is newer than the board's, unless the running code is the main checkout's, judged by where the running bin lives and not by the folder the command runs in. The refusal names the versions and the next step (merge first, or test against a throwaway board). There is no undocumented override. Commands that only read the spec, such as spec check, don't open the board at all. Tests run a newer schema from a linked worktree, including that worktree's bin run with the main checkout as its folder, and check the shared board is unchanged and the refusal is named; and check that the main checkout's code still upgrades in place. The gate passes.

items.title: Fixture commits carry their own identity, so CI passes
items.criterion: test/row-decisions.test.js passes where git can't detect an identity, because its fixture sets its own identity after stripping GIT_* variables. bin/run-tests.js makes a test that leans on the machine's identity fail locally, even one that strips every GIT_* variable and sets a new HOME, the way it fails on GitHub's Linux runners.
items.brief:
Main's CI on GitHub has failed on Linux since 4f3181e. One cause is this item; the other is #205's Chrome flake.

Files:
- test/row-decisions.test.js: sandbox() puts the fixture's GIT_AUTHOR_*, GIT_COMMITTER_* and GIT_CONFIG_* into the env, then passes the env through personEnvironment(), which deletes every GIT_* key. Fixture commits fall back to git's detected identity. A Mac account has a full name, so it passes locally. GitHub's runner user has none, so `git commit` dies with "Author identity unknown … empty ident name". Set the identity and config after the strip, in sandbox() and in run(), because run() strips again.
- bin/run-tests.js: its useConfigOnly guard rides on GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, which this fixture strips, so the local gate never saw the problem. Make the guard survive a test that strips every GIT_* variable and sets a new HOME. One way: a git shim in the runner's shims dir that runs the real git with -c user.useConfigOnly=true.

Test:
- The item's check fails before the fixture fix and passes after it.
- Mutation: with the runner change and the old fixture, `node bin/run-tests.js test/row-decisions.test.js` fails locally with "Author identity unknown".
- The whole gate passes, and GitHub CI's Linux jobs pass this test.

items.title: The relay refuses clients too old to judge agent moves
items.criterion: Every relay request from the CLI declares its engine version, and the relay refuses a client below the minimum engine version for that board (3 once the board has any agent token) with a refusal that says to upgrade pullboard. An honest old client therefore can't be fooled by a forged record it doesn't know to refuse. Tests prove it: an engine-2 client is refused on a board with an agent token, before it reads any records, and is served on a board without one; an engine-3 client is served on both. The gate passes.
items.brief:
Found by tests-27 while accepting #236 (relay replay attributes moves to the authenticated sender). Read its verdict note with pullboard show 236: every gap there is proven on two real clients, and its probes are a good harness. #236 is merged; build on main. Run relay tests against throwaway boards only, never the shared board.

Gap C, relay deploy blocker: the engine bump can't protect old replicas, because whoever seals a record picks its engine number. Proven: a v2 replica (the ff714cf build) applied a forged engine-2 coordinator accept from remote-1, and v3 refused it. Before agent tokens are issued on the deployed relay (app.pullboard.dev), every linked device must run engine 3 or later. The opaque relay can't see that inside sealed records, so the client must declare its engine version on every request, and the relay must refuse older clients with an upgrade message. It's protecting honest old clients from being fooled, not stopping a lying one.

items.title: Submit and accept refuse work that won't merge into the trunk

Both checks touch no worktree and no index. Tests cover a clean merge accepted, a conflicting submit refused with its files named, and an accept refused after the trunk moves into a conflict. The gate passes.

items.title: pullboard land: one sequencer is the only path to main
items.criterion: pullboard land merges verified items in verdict order in a landing worktree, refuses stacked unverified work, skips and names conflicts, gates the batch once as a landing, and on green pushes, records merged and emits a main-moved event; on a red that reproduces it bisects to the culprit, lands the green items and names the failing tests on the culprit; a red that passes alone files a flake against its test and lands nothing until the test is fixed or the person records an expiring waiver, and nothing retries; batches are board records a new coordinator can adopt; run twice it records once. Under a waiver the gate still runs every test: land records a landing proof at the exact batch tree naming each failing test and the live waiver that covers it, and the pre-push hook accepts that proof only when every failure it names is covered by a waiver that has not expired, without writing an ordinary green stamp and without any hook bypass. This first stage does not refuse other pushes: the existing gate-stamped push and pullboard merged keep working, and refusing every path but land is a later item.
items.brief:
The person, 9 Oct: yes to a sequencer, the one path to main, so landing stops depending on a coordinator doing it by hand. Tonight the coordinator was the sequencer: batching accepted items, waiting in the gate queue, finding the culprit by hand when a batch went red (one verified item broke 38 tests only when the gate ran over SSH), rebuilding the batch and re-pushing. Each cycle cost 15-45 minutes. This folds in #278 (batch records), which gets withdrawn in its favour.

pullboard land [--max N] [--dry-run], coordinator only:
1. Take verified items that have no merged record, in verdict order, respecting --after. Refuse one whose landed range would carry another item's unverified or rejected commit (STACKED_UNVERIFIED #N).
2. In a landing worktree under the board's git dir, never the main checkout, merge each one with --no-ff and a valid header: "type(merge): <title> [ids]", lowercased and cut at a word boundary to 72 characters. Skip a conflicting item and name its files, so the integrator gets it.
3. Run the full gate once for the batch, as a landing (it goes first in the gate queue, from #285).
4. Green: push the tip, record merged for each item at the merge commit that first contains it, emit a main-moved event with the new sha, and fast-forward the main checkout when it is clean.
5. Red: rerun only the failing test files, alone. Failing again is a real red: split the batch in half and gate each half until the culprit is found, land the green items, and post a fact on the culprit naming the failing tests. Passing alone is a flake (the person, 9 Oct: no retries, PB5): file it once against that test, and stop. Nothing lands until the test is fixed or the person records an expiring waiver for it (pullboard land --waive <test> --until <date> --reason "...", person-only). Nothing retries.
6. The batch is a board record (tip, items, state, owner, log path), so pullboard resume shows it and a new coordinator can adopt it.

- src/cli.js (the land command)
- src/board.js (batch records and the main-moved event)

items.title: A short code chip never breaks across lines, so main's CI is green
items.criterion: Inline code chips in shouts and briefs stay whole: a short chip such as --flag never breaks inside itself at any width, so at 375 and 1280 it is a single fragment, display inline, narrower than half its line, including when it falls at a line's end. A code span longer than its line can still wrap and never overflows the screen width. The real Chrome test that checks this passes on CI's Linux and macOS runners.
items.brief:
Main's CI is red on all four jobs (run on e4c17af) in #271's own test, real Chrome styles shout code and item text without growing linked lines [N26], at test/cockpit.test.js:3798. The failure: '375px shout code is a compact chip: {"display":"inline","width":237.9375,"lineWidth":243.609375}'. The chip is display inline, as #271 intended, but on CI's Chrome and fonts the short chip --flag lands at a line's end and breaks after "--", so its bounding box spans two line fragments, nearly the full line wide. The Studio's Chrome wrapped the same line differently, so the landing gate passed.

A short code chip should never break inside itself. Keep chips whole (for example white-space: nowrap on code.inline), while a code span too long for the line can still wrap rather than overflow the phone width. The test measures the chip's own line fragments (getClientRects), so a legitimately wrapping long span isn't mistaken for a bar.

items.criterion: In a checkout whose primary HEAD is detached (verify's private clone, CI, a rebase in progress), pullboard spec check and spec --json read the collision baseline from the trunk ref and report rows and errors, with known duplicates still warnings; an attached primary checkout is unchanged; with neither a branch nor a trunk ref, the refusal names the fix.

Reproduce: clone the repo, `git checkout --detach origin/main`, run `node bin/pullboard.js spec check`. It refuses; it should print the rows and errors.

Rule: when the primary checkout is detached, read the collision baseline from the trunk ref, resolved exactly as #252's merge check resolves it. An attached primary checkout keeps using its branch, unchanged. With no branch and no resolvable trunk, keep the refusal, naming the fix.

items.title: Test fixtures never kill a child on a fixed clock, and a failed child names itself
items.criterion: No core-owned test fixture kills a CLI or git child on a fixed short timeout except where the bound is the assertion and is named; the per-test timeout bounds hangs; every fixture helper that runs a child reports, on a nonzero exit or signal, the command, status or signal, elapsed time and stderr.
items.brief:
Capture, Studio landing gate on d3e42e3 (14:28Z, load about 10): test/person.test.js:291 "[B26,S5] an agent shell cannot append a person sign-off but a plain shell can" failed after 10.07 s with a bare "null !== 0" at person.test.js:78. The sandbox run() helper (person.test.js:65) spawns the CLI with spawnSync timeout: 10_000, so under load `pullboard init` was killed: status null, signal SIGTERM, no stderr in the message. Alone on the same tree: 5/5 green.

It's a class, not one test. About 51 fixed kill timeouts in spawnSync/execFile calls across about 20 test files (git grep "timeout: [0-9]+_?000" in test/). Since #287, the test runner fails a hung test by name within minutes, so a fixture-level kill clock adds nothing but load flakes, and when it fires it hides the cause.

Rule: a CLI or git child in a core-owned test fixture is never killed by a fixed short clock. Either drop the per-call timeout and let #287's per-test timeout bound the hang, or, where a per-call bound is part of what the test asserts, derive it from the work and name it. Every helper that runs a child reports, when the child didn't exit 0: the command, its exit status or signal, elapsed time and stderr, never a bare "null !== 0".

Files:
- core-owned tests under test/ (not test/cockpit.test.js, which is the view lane's) and any shared fixture helper they use

Test:
- "a fixture child killed or failed names its command, signal and stderr": a helper running a child that sleeps past a deliberate bound reports the command, SIGTERM, the elapsed time and the stderr. Removing the detail turns the test red.
- git grep for fixed spawnSync kill timeouts in core-owned tests returns only the ones listed in the submit with their reason.

items.title: pullboard.dev opens the boards on this machine
items.criterion: A person on this machine opens their board on the hosted Pullboard page, the page app.pullboard.dev already serves for the relay, and on this machine that page talks straight to the local view on 127.0.0.1 instead of the relay: no tunnel, no copied link, and no board data leaves the machine (the site serves only the page). One UI, two transports: on this machine, the local view; on any other device, the relay as today. N26 stays whole: every API request the hosted page sends carries the view's per-session secret in the x-pullboard-key header the view already reads, never in a URL query. The page gets the secret without a copied link by a round trip: it sends the browser on a top-level visit to the local view, which sends it straight back to https://app.pullboard.dev only, with the secret in the URL fragment; the page keeps the secret for that tab and removes it from the address bar at once. Any site can start the round trip, but the secret only ever reaches app.pullboard.dev, and the round-trip page refuses to be framed. When the view restarts with a new secret, the page repeats the round trip by itself. Before the browser's own local-network prompt (measured in Chrome and Firefox on 13 Oct), the page tells the person in one line why it will appear. Whenever the page cannot reach the local view (no view running, the browser's permission denied, a browser that blocks it, or an installed CLI whose local API is too old), it says which of these it knows and links the local view, which always matches the installed version; Safari's own behavior is recorded as a fact when a person measures it and does not block this item. The local view answers its own origin and https://app.pullboard.dev only, with CORS for that origin and Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true on the preflight; it refuses every other origin with a plain error; it refuses any request whose Host header is not 127.0.0.1 or localhost on its port, which stops DNS rebinding; and it accepts writes only as JSON from an allowed origin. The local session link keeps working as today. A real-Chrome test, "a pullboard.dev page reads the local board", serves a local stand-in page under an allowed origin, makes the round trip, and reads the board through the view's API; "a foreign origin or wrong Host is refused by the local view" shows a foreign origin, a wrong Host header, and an allowed origin without the secret each refused; "the local view hands its secret only to the hosted page" asserts the round trip redirects only to the allowed origin with the secret only in the fragment. items.criterion: A socket that closes under a request fails that request, never the process. On Node 24.21 (bundled undici 7.29.1), undici's writeH1 calls socket.setTypeOfService(request.typeOfService) on each new socket before its first write, and Node throws the setsockopt error; on macOS that error escaped as an uncaughtException and failed the running test twice in Studio landing gates on 13 Oct: "an agent's pullboard view prints its link and returns" (test/e2e-view.test.js:60) at dfa205f, and "pullboard view uses its fixed default port and reuses its authenticated listener" (test/view-port.test.js:220) at b9b975f, both "setTypeOfService EINVAL" from writeH1. The same path runs in pullboard itself wherever it fetches a local view: src/view-session.js and src/cli.js's view probe (src/serve.js, in the view lane, gets a companion item if it cannot use the shared guard). ROOT-CAUSE STATUS: NOT PROVEN. Measured: the stack, the Node and undici versions, and that undici calls setTypeOfService unguarded. Not known: which close reaches the socket first, or why macOS returns EINVAL there; quick reproductions (the peer destroying or resetting on connect, with and without a busy client) did not trigger it. First, a deterministic test reproduces the escape on a real socket at undici's first write and shows the uncaught exception. Then pullboard's own local fetch callers and the test helpers that fetch a view survive it: the request fails as a closed or refused connection, and nothing escapes. items.title: The phone view never waits without a deadline at startup
items.criterion: Part of #899 (core-351's audit, 17096): in src/cockpit.js, connectLocal awaits navigator.permissions.query before its bounded fetch, loadTransport awaits import(configuredTransportModule) with no deadline, and the phone shell can be cleared before the cockpit's first board render. After this item, on a phone connectLocal returns unreachable at once without the permission query or the fetch; the transport import is bounded by a cleared timer (15 s), and a timed-out or failed import shows visible guidance in the phone shell; the cockpit calls createTransport({ waitForRender: true }) and calls transport.didRender?.() after its first successful render and after each successful refresh, and both are harmless with a transport that has neither (the transport on main today), proven by a case for that; each change is proven by a case that fails without it; the C9 count does not rise; and the gate passes.
items.brief:
The view part of #899: two awaits in src/cockpit.js on the phone's startup path have no deadline. Found by core-351's #899 audit (17096); core-351 handles the relay side (approvals off the transport's path, bounded HTTP, IndexedDB and crypto startup reads) and merges this item's commit before #899's final proof.

1. connectLocal awaits navigator.permissions.query before its bounded fetch. A phone never runs the local view (the code already says so), so on a phone connectLocal returns unreachable at once, without the permission query or the fetch.
2. loadTransport awaits import(configuredTransportModule) with no deadline. Bound it with a timer that is cleared when the import settles; on timeout or failure the phone shell shows visible guidance (what failed and what to do), never an empty page.

The deadline for I/O is 15 s (the existing snapshot catch-up ceiling), separate from the 3 s first-text requirement, which #897 already meets by painting first. src/cockpit.js is over 1500 lines and its C9 count can only fall, so the change must not add a 100-line bucket.

Proven on Linux by the frozen check, which runs the case three times in a node:22.13.1-bookworm container through the MacBook's Docker. At main 6d936804 it fails there 3/3 with "a group signal really answered EPERM before the release", as GitHub CI did on Linux 22.13 and 24 (run 39430589416), while the same tree passes 2/2 on macOS. Two controls are recorded as facts: with the OS-dependent forcing removed the case still sees EPERM, and with #888's retry reverted the case goes red, each on Linux in the same container. items.brief:
Follow-up to #927 (merged 0e457b78), whose bar said a Linux CI red reopens it; merged items cannot reopen, so this item carries it. GitHub CI for 48f2facb (run 39430589416) fails this case on linux 22.13 3/3 and linux 24 3/3 with "a group signal really answered EPERM before the release: false !== true".

Root-cause status: NOT PROVEN. Measured: on one tree (git archive of 6d936804), macOS passes 2/2 and a node:22.13.1-bookworm container fails 2/2 with the same assertion. Not known: why the eperm-once preload in test/runner-parent-death-fixture.js never answers on Linux. It answers on the second real (non-zero) signal to one process group. Candidates are that the worker sends only one real group signal on Linux, because the group is gone before the retry; that the preload is not loaded in the process that signals on Linux; or that the group id differs. Discriminating control: log every process.kill call the preload sees, with pid and signal, on both OSes in the same tree. The first divergence names the cause.

Run Linux on the MacBook with Docker (colima is running; it mounts only paths under the home directory). Example: copy the tree under the home directory, then docker run --rm -v <dir>:/w -w /w node:22.13.1-bookworm sh -c 'git config --global --add safe.directory /w && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.name=x -c user.email=x@x commit -qm snap && node bin/run-tests.js --test-name-pattern "group signal answers EPERM" test/runners.test.js'. The frozen check does exactly this, three times.

Files: test/runner-parent-death-fixture.js (the eperm-once preload and the launcher), test/runners.test.js if the case's forcing moves, and src/ only if the divergence proves the worker itself behaves wrongly on Linux.

Test: test/runners.test.js "a queued run executes on a registered runner and its result comes back [C7] (parent death drains its worker when a group signal answers EPERM)" passes 3/3 on Linux in the container and on macOS, and still asserts that the EPERM really fired and the lease was released.

items.title: A reopened item waits for its builder first, as a board setting
items.criterion: With pullboard.json "claim.reopenFirstRefusalMinutes": N set (off by default, on for this board at 30), an item reopened by a rejection, a landing failure or a trunk conflict can be claimed only by its builder for N minutes after the reopen. Another seat's claim in that window is refused with REOPEN_HELD_FOR_BUILDER, naming the builder and the time the window ends. The builder is told once, at the reopen, that the item waits for it. After the window, or if the builder releases it, anyone may claim. Without the setting, claims work exactly as today. Proven in test/claim-reopen.test.js (new; test/board.test.js is at 1445 of its 1500 lines) by a new case, "a reopened item waits for its builder first", covering the refusal inside the window, the builder's claim inside it, and another seat's claim after it; the case fails before the change. The changelog line is recorded as a note fact.
items.brief:
Twice on 20 Oct, a builder did not reclaim its item after a reopen and another seat claimed it, so two seats built the same fix. #919: core-364's lapsed claim versus core-413. #814: the train reopened it at 21:25Z, core-427 claimed it at 21:56Z, and core-417's fix was already ready. In both cases the original builder held a complete or nearly complete fix. A short first-refusal window after a reopen keeps the builder's context and prevents the duplicate. It ships opt-in because it changes who may claim (the board's rule: behavior changes are settings, off by default, on for our own board).

Files: src/claims.js (or wherever the claim move checks ownership), src/machine.js (declare REOPEN_HELD_FOR_BUILDER on the claim move), src/config.js (the setting), docs/api.md, test/claim-reopen.test.js (new; test/board.test.js is at 1445 of its 1500 lines). If recording the window on the reopen event needs an engine number, ask the coordinator; the next unused is 64.

Test: test/claim-reopen.test.js (new; test/board.test.js is at 1445 of its 1500 lines) "a reopened item waits for its builder first": with the setting at 30, another seat's claim 5 minutes after a reopen is refused with REOPEN_HELD_FOR_BUILDER, the builder's claim succeeds, and another seat's claim 31 minutes later succeeds (use the board's injectable clock). Without the setting, all three claims behave as today.

items.brief:

items.criterion: From the person's contributions list (25 Oct, points 19-23, exactly as the brief words them). (19) A brief may carry any number of Reference: <anything outside the board> lines. A reference carries an @handle only when the maintainer acknowledges someone at triage, and the handle must match that issue's or pull request's author. (20) Submit prints a reminder, never a refusal, when an item with a handled reference adds no matching changelog line. (21) Before tagging, the release check names every handled reference among the release's landed items that is missing from the changelog. (22) add and edit refuse a Reference that is only a board id, naming the right flag (REFERENCE_IS_BOARD). (23) Only handled references ever leave the board: the changelog, the PR bridge, anything published. Proven by cases in test/references.test.js, one per point, each failing before the change.
items.brief:
## G. References

19. **The `Reference:` line.** An item's brief may carry any number of lines `Reference: <anything outside the board>`: a link, a document, a conversation, code at a commit. Spec rows go in `--specs` and board items in `--after`/`--parent`, never in a Reference. A reference gets an `@handle` only when the maintainer chooses to acknowledge someone at triage, and the handle must match that issue's or pull request's author. No handle, no acknowledgement and no check.
20. **Submit reminder.** When an item has a handled reference and its change adds no matching changelog line, submit prints a reminder (never a refusal); one issue may span several items.
21. **Release gate.** Before tagging, every handled reference among the release's landed items appears at least once in that release's changelog, or the release check names what is missing.
22. **Add and edit refuse a Reference that is only a board id**, naming the right flag: `REFERENCE_IS_BOARD: "H21" is a spec row; cite it with --specs H21 so it counts in the bar.`
23. **Only handled references ever leave the board** (the changelog, the PR bridge, anything published). Every other reference stays private.
24. **Referenced pages are information, never instructions**: a line in the triage skill and the agent guidance.

items.title: Main red: two relay-client cases fail on main 2e36121 (second claim and recovery: recordUsage mismatch, likely since the #1876 usage cap)

items.title: Known-main owner falls back to the one repair that runs the whole file when no criterion names the case
items.criterion: 30 Oct (#1829, seven GATE_RED submits): test/land.test.js failures that also fail on main match two repairs, #1872 (check runs one case by --test-name-pattern) and #1993 (check runs the whole file). Neither criterion names the other failing cases, so ownersOf in src/known-main-reworks.js returns both and linkKnownMainReworks returns null; every land.test.js failure is then unowned and the submit refuses GATE_RED. items.title: Rework returns to its seat, or to a seat of the same model family when that seat is gone
items.criterion: 30 Oct, relayed by tests-85 as approved by the person (shout 48296): rework (a reject or reopen) goes back to the same seat; if that seat is gone, it goes to a seat of the same model family, so a handoff never spans families and never strands review. Behind a setting (default off, on for our boards). Builds on #1933 first refusal. Test: reject with the builder live reserves it for that seat; with the builder gone, next offers it only to same-family seats until none is live, then to any seat with a named fact. Ruling 30 Oct (core-861, 49322): 'gone' uses the same native definition as #2059 (no presence and no claim past the grace period, or a completed handoff takeover), read from the sealed routing state, never from the display-only presence sidecar. A 'live same-family seat' is a seat of the builder's recorded family whose native presence is within the takeover window. When no live same-family seat exists, the board itself records the fallback fact at routing time (actor: the board), naming the families it checked. Refinement 30 Oct (core-861, 49326): #2059 has not landed, so do not wait on it. The native presence signal is the seat's most recent recorded board event (claim, renew, submit, verdict or release in the event log), which is sealed and replayable: a seat is live when that event falls inside the takeover window, and gone when it falls outside the grace period and the seat holds no claim. When #2059 lands, both items read the same rule.

items.title: cells-plan places a process entry file in the app cell that composes it
items.criterion: 30 Oct (core-714, 48837/48843, for #2032): process entry files (check-baseline worker, landing worker and candidate, main-audit worker, nudge and scheduler, source-advance, baseline launcher) are composition roots that open the board, but cells-plan cannot say so: --place rejects bin/ paths for a cell, and files marked 'stays' have no owner, so their native-board imports read as upward edges from lower cells. Ruling 30 Oct (core-714, 48907): cells-submit-checks may accept an accepted row moving to a later cell only for a source-validated explicit process entry (the --entry placement this item adds); every other move to a later cell, and a library file marked --entry, is still refused. items.title: Browser tests leave no Chrome behind: runners quit Chrome cleanly and sweep orphaned code-sign clones
items.criterion: 30 Oct (the person, via another agent's disk audit: 265 GB of orphaned Google Chrome code-sign clones, about 190 at 1.4 GB each, from Oct 20-26; coordinator count 30 Oct 17:5xZ: runners .51 1110, .52 1068, .53 1066, .54 528 clones in /private/var/folders/*/*/X/com.google.Chrome.code_sign_clone; .55 4, .56 2). Fix: the browser test harness quits Chrome through its own shutdown before any kill, and runner cleanup (with #2059's maintenance sweep) removes code-sign clone directories that no running Chrome process uses and that are older than one hour, logging one line per sweep with the count and space freed. Never touch a clone a live Chrome uses. Test: a fixture killed browser leaves a clone that the sweep removes; a clone held by a live process is kept. Ruling 30 Oct (core-804, 49076): build the Chrome sweep and the graceful shutdown independently of #2059; the sweep runs from runner cleanup on its own schedule and does not wait for #2059. When #2059 lands, its maintenance run may call this sweep, which is that item's concern, not this one's.

items.title: Model tiers: each project maps routine, standard and escalation work to the models it chooses
items.criterion: Generalizes #2088 (person-approved 30 Oct coordinator split). For any project: pullboard.json declares model tiers (for example routine, standard, escalation), each naming one or more models by vendor and id, including a self-hosted endpoint (any OpenAI-compatible or MCP-reachable URL) as well as hosted vendors. The board routes work by tier, not by vendor name: mechanical coordination runs as code with no model; routine work (item writing in the numbered-clause format of #2050, narrow builds, reviews of small items) goes to the routine tier; escalated rulings go to the escalation tier; and an item can be pinned to a tier. No vendor or model name is hard-coded in src/. Defaults ship for the common hosted vendors and favour the smallest model that passes, with escalation after two bounces. Tests: a project with only a self-hosted endpoint routes every tier to it; a project mapping routine to a small model sends item writing there; an unknown tier refuses with its name. Proof on runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: The per-file ratchet follows a file through a rename
items.criterion: For any project: the submit-time per-file ratchet (doctrine counts compared per changed path, for example the file-size cap) maps each renamed path to its origin with git rename detection, the same similarity rule git uses, and compares the renamed file against its origin count, so moving an existing file is never charged as new problems. A file that gains problems in the move still refuses as today. Found on this repo 31 Oct: #1574 moved src/relay.js (1769 lines, 3 over-cap problems already) to packages/link/src/shell/relay.js (1714 lines); the ratchet read --no-renames, saw a new path with 3 problems and refused RATCHET_ROSE though the total fell. This is a guard used at submit, so it lands before #1574. Tests: a renamed over-cap file with the same or fewer problems passes; a renamed file that gains a problem refuses; a genuinely new over-cap file refuses (negative controls). Proof on runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: Build, submit and review test runs shard their files across free runner slots
items.criterion: Person ruling 31 Oct (via tests-85, 51520). For any project with runners: today build, submit and review test runs always use 1 runner slot (last 24h on this repo: focused p90 6.4 min, test 3.6, submit 2.5, review 2.2) while most of about 54 slots sit idle. After this item those runs split their selected test files across free runner slots, balanced by measured per-file time, reusing the landing-shard machinery; a run uses at most the free slots and never starves landings (landing stays first in the queue order); one result and one receipt come back, identical in content to a single-slot run. Tests: a run with N files on a fixture with several free slots splits them balanced by recorded times and returns one combined result; with one free slot it runs as today; a failing file in any shard fails the run with that file named. Proof on runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: Routing is a board move with one coordinator; relayed rulings become proposals on their items
items.criterion: For any project. Found 31 Oct: a person ruling arrived as a shout relayed by one agent (combine five items), the coordinator filed a combined item for it, and another builder had already started combining them under a different item; two routing sources acted on messages and nothing on the board said who owned the work. After this item: (1) one seat holds the coordinator role per board at a time (pullboard coordinate takes it, a second attempt is refused naming the holder, and the role is released on exit or stall like a claim); (2) every routing change is a board move with a recorded actor and reason: assigning or pinning work, forming or changing a block (#2202), folding items, holding, and accepting a person ruling; (3) a routing request from any other seat, including a relayed person ruling, is recorded as a proposal bound to the items it names, and the coordinator accepts or declines it on the board (accepted person rulings also land in the rulings ledg … (cut; --detail shows the whole line) Added (person, 1 Nov): an assignment the coordinator makes is binding. The seat's next returns it, a claim on any other build item is refused with the assignment named until the seat claims or declines it with a reason, and an urgent assignment reaches the seat's watch feed as an interrupt.

items.title: Cells cut: state core files stop importing MACHINE, ENGINE_VERSION and correctedBar from the state shell
items.criterion: Found 31 Oct by the state shim removal (#1679): core files item-edit-bar, item-list, work-order and focus-milestone import MACHINE, ENGINE_VERSION and correctedBar from the state shell through src/machine.js and src/corrected-bar.js, so those shims are kept. After this item the pure values these core files need come from the state pure core.js (moving pure definitions there unchanged) or are passed in as ports, no core file imports a shell module, the two kept shims are deleted, and node bin/cells-plan.js --check and --cuts report nothing new. Standing cut ruling; proof on runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: Submit and landing run only the tests of unsealed packages, plus contracts at changed front doors
items.criterion: Implements RFC 0006 amendment row A3 (approved 31 Oct); proof on runners at Node 22.22.2; journeys run per landing batch. 1. Selection: a change touching one package runs that package's tests plus the contract tests of its changed front door; a change to a widely imported front door runs its importers' tests; every sealed package's tests are skipped with its seal receipt named in the output. 2. Guard: the gate computes the required set as every unsealed package's tests plus every changed front door's contract tests, and refuses the submit when any required test is missing from the run's proof files, whatever plan.skipped lists. 3. Control (person-agreed 31 Oct): in test/seal-selection.test.js a real runSubmitGate run is refused when an importer test is dropped from units and proof files with skipped unchanged, and again when a changed front door's contract test is dropped the same way.

items.title: A person with no clone and no terminal gets a repository and runners that we host
items.criterion: A person with no clone, no terminal and no installed tools starts a project and gets a repository and Runners that we host, with nothing to set up on their own machine. Their Agents build and their Criterion checks run on those hosted Runners, and a finished item lands in the hosted repository. Proven by named tests that start from an empty account and reach a landed item without any local clone or terminal command, and by a proof run on Runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: Board tools read git once per command: pre-commit, the shim tool and the cells checks finish in seconds
items.criterion: Person-approved 31 Oct speed plan, step 3 (batch the tools). Measured by the 31 Oct profiler: cells-plan --remove-shims took about 121 seconds a run from a per-cell loop that re-reads the repository; pre-commit about 5 seconds. Time bars are proved by bounded work, not clock asserts, because the wall-clock policy bans literal time margins in tests (coordinator ruling, 1 Nov). After this item: pre-commit on a 300-file fixture commit makes a bounded number of git calls that does not grow per file, with the same refusals as before; the internal cells tools (bin/ only, never shipped) read the repository once per run: --remove-shims builds exactly one inventory per run however many repoint passes it takes, and --check and --moved reuse one inventory. Tests: a counter shows one inventory per --remove-shims run; the 300-file pre-commit fixture asserts its git-call bound and its refusals; elapsed times are logged for the record, never asserted. Proof on runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: Cells cut: browser-facing relay code reads a pages entry that loads no Node built-ins
items.criterion: Internal restructure (never ships as user behavior). Found 31 Oct on #1692: the browser-facing relay importers of src/relay-presentation.js cannot use the pages front door (packages/pages/index.js), because it loads packages/pages/src/shell/relay-presentation.js, which imports node:path, and the relay parity tests fail in the browser shape. So the shim stays. After this item, the browser-safe part of relay-presentation lives in packages/pages core (no node: imports), the browser importers read packages/pages/core.js, the Node-only part stays shell, and src/relay-presentation.js is deleted. Tests: test/relay-parity*.test.js green; a guard that no module reachable from the relay browser entry imports a node: built-in. Proof on runners at Node 22.22.2.

items.title: Main red: 16 test files fail on main with MILESTONE_PLACED since computed placement (#2235) landed
items.criterion: Found 1 Nov by the Claude reviewer of #2238: 16 of 71 importer test files fail identically on main b0c48e1fa with a MILESTONE_PLACED refusal in their fixtures, because fixtures place items in milestones by hand and #2235 now places them by rule. After this item every such fixture either relies on the board's placement or passes --reason for a deliberate override, all 16 files pass on main, and no assertion is weakened; the item lists the 16 files. Scope (coordinator, 1 Nov): the view-lane files belong to #2267 and the flow-report cache defect to #2268; a case owned by either passes this bar when it fails identically on main and the submit note names it. Out of scope: any case that fails identically on main for a cause other than MILESTONE_PLACED; the submit note names those cases. In scope, every MILESTONE_PLACED case passes, and no case may fail where main passes. A MILESTONE_PLACED case that now gets past placement and fails a later assertion counts as fixed here: the later failure was masked on main, and the submit note names each one for a follow-up item.
items.brief: One root cause behind 16 red files; #2235's own tests passed because they never ran these importers.

items.title: Main red: a milestone override leaves the item in both milestones in the cached and replayed flow report
items.criterion: Found by core-947 on #2259 (fact on #2259, log /tmp/pb-2259-core-verify.log). When a milestone override moves an item from A to B, board state shows it in B only, but the cached and replayed flow report still lists it in both, and shipping A leaves A and C in the projection. After this item the cached, replayed and live flow reports agree with board state after any override, and a fixture proves the move, the replay and the ship case.

items.title: Browser admission stops classing source-scanning tests as browser-bound when cell barrels reach browser modules
items.criterion: Found 1 Nov by core-951 on #2273 (fact 084cc96e): since the cells moves, packages/gate/tests/gui-marker-guard.test.js, test/cell-lint-guard.test.js, test/shared-wait-guard.test.js and test/view-test-policy.test.js are classed browser-bound because their import graphs reach broad cell barrels, which wastes browser slots and fails the affected-tests guard case. After this item a test is browser-bound only when it can actually launch a browser (a call or side-effect analysis, or a public-entry design that keeps browser executors out of non-browser front doors), the four scanners are classed source-only, and every real browser test stays browser-bound; fixtures cover both. It also carries #2273's stale guard census fix (from d14d84c80, core-951's commit 1fef204e), since the two must land together for the affected-tests guard case to pass.
items.brief: A cells consequence: barrels widen import graphs. Fixing it also frees browser slots.

items.title: Submit's local stages (composition, cell checks, static, doctrine) run on a runner, not the builder's shared machine
items.criterion: Speed plan D1, re-scoped by measurement. On 1 Nov the cell checks took about 13-16 minutes of #2251's submit (the cell compiler was still running at 13 minutes) while doctrine took about one. After this item: (1) submit's cell checks record a receipt keyed by the tree, the check's definition hash (its command, its import closure and the config it reads, as in #2230) and the board cuts they read, and a matching receipt is reused by a later submit of the same tree (review and landing do not run cell checks today, so they gain no new check); (2) on a miss, they check only the cells the change touches plus the cells that import them, never the whole repository; (3) submit prints each local stage's elapsed time; (4) a fixture shows an unchanged tree reusing the receipt, a one-cell change checking only that cell and its importers, and a cut change invalidating the receipt. Offloading cell checks to a runner is a follow-up only if a measured submit still spends over 2 minutes in them.

items.title: Runner cleanup names the process it waits on, and land.test.js leaves no detached descendants behind
items.criterion: Measured 1 Nov: RUNNER_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT stalled submits of #1872, #1993 and #2259 on runners .52, .53 and .56 for up to an hour, with no stray Pullboard processes left afterward, so the runner was waiting on test descendants that outlived the run. After this item: (1) a cleanup timeout records the pid, command and start time of every process it waited on, in the receipt and the refusal; (2) every test in test/land.test.js and test/landing-shards.test.js that starts detached processes reaps them before it ends, using the existing drain helpers; (3) a fixture starts a detached child, ends the test, and shows cleanup finishing without a timeout.
items.brief: Person, 1 Nov: every lock and timeout should be recorded and diagnosed. Pairs with #2257's land.test.js split.

items.title: Submit's automatic shouts fit the shout limit, so a long note can never fail a recorded submit
items.criterion: Seen 1 Nov on #2251, #2277, #2287 and #2272: the submit ran its gate (sometimes for 18+ minutes), then its automatic shout exceeded 400 characters and the command exited SHOUT_TOO_LONG, so builders could not tell whether the submit was recorded. After this item every automatic shout from submit, verify and land is shortened to fit with a pointer to show, the command's exit code reflects only the move itself, and a fixture with a 2,000-character note submits with exit 0 and one shout under the limit.

items.title: Submit's cells check runs in under a minute: only the touched cells
items.criterion: Seen 1 Nov: #2251's submit spent 461 s in the cells check inside its queued gate, after an earlier attempt spent ~17 min in cells preflight; other handoffs took 475 s, 67 s, 28 s (0.6 s when reused). After this item the cells check on a candidate proves only the cells its diff touches plus their direct importers, reusing receipts for the rest; a fixture with a one-cell change on a repo with many cells finishes the cells stage in under 60 s and still refuses a new cut in the touched cell.

items.title: Rulings are recorded, attached to their item and queryable, and repeats become doctrine drafts
items.criterion: Corey 1 Nov: judgement calls should accumulate and be queryable. Seen 1 Nov: the coordinator sent 244 --kind decision shouts in a day, mixing routing ('claim #2310 now') with real rulings ('direct importers include pure forwarding modules' on #2313, 'conservative all-cells fallback for root-tool stays'), and none are linked to their item or findable later. After this item 'pullboard rule <id> "<question>" "<answer>"' records a ruling on the item: it shows in pullboard show and in next's instruction for that item, 'pullboard rulings [text]' lists rulings across the board with item, author and date, and a ruling whose question matches an earlier one surfaces the earlier answer first; rulings that recur on three items are listed as doctrine drafts for the person to approve, never applied automatically. Fixtures cover record, show, search, the repeat surfacing and the draft listing.
